title: 419. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Angle Sum and Difference Formulas
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: State the formula for the sine of a sum of two angles.
questions.question: For all angles \(A\) and \(B\), \(\sin(A+B)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: The sum formula is \(\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B\). The expression with a minus sign is \(\sin(A-B)\). A quick check with \(A=B=45^\circ\): the sum formula gives \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1=\sin 90^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: State the formula for the cosine of a sum of two angles.
questions.question: For all angles \(A\) and \(B\), \(\cos(A+B)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: The sum formula is \(\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B\). The expression with a plus sign is \(\cos(A-B)\). A check with \(A=B=45^\circ\): \(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=0=\cos 90^\circ\).
questions.hint: For cosine the sign in the formula is opposite to the sign between the angles; test with \(A=B=45^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sine exactly by writing the angle as a sum of standard angles.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\sin 75^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(75^\circ=45^\circ+30^\circ\). Then \(\sin 75^\circ=\sin 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ+\cos 45^\circ\sin 30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\approx 0.966\). The value with a minus sign is \(\sin 15^\circ\approx 0.259\).
questions.hint: Split \(75^\circ\) into two standard angles and apply the sine sum formula.

questions.concept: Exact cosine of an obtuse angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cosine exactly by writing the angle as a sum of standard angles.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\cos 105^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(105^\circ=60^\circ+45^\circ\). Then \(\cos 105^\circ=\cos 60^\circ\cos 45^\circ-\sin 60^\circ\sin 45^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{6}}{4}\approx -0.259\). The value is negative, as expected for an angle in Quadrant II.
questions.hint: Split \(105^\circ\) into two standard angles; the cosine of a Quadrant II angle must be negative.

questions.concept: Tangent of a sum from two tangents
questions.learningObjective: Apply the tangent sum formula to given tangent values.
questions.question: Angles \(A\) and \(B\) satisfy \(\tan A=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\tan B=\frac{1}{3}\). What is \(\tan(A+B)\)?
questions.explanation: Use \(\tan(A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{6}}=\frac{5/6}{5/6}=1\). Using \(1+\tan A\tan B\) in the denominator gives \(\frac{5/6}{7/6}=\frac{5}{7}\), which is the value of \(\tan(A-B)\) with a sign error in the numerator.
questions.hint: The denominator of the tangent sum formula is \(1-\tan A\tan B\).

questions.concept: Shifting sine by a quarter turn
questions.learningObjective: Simplify a sine with a shifted argument using the sum formula.
questions.question: For every real \(x\), \(\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: By the sum formula, \(\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=\sin x\cdot 0+\cos x\cdot 1=\cos x\). The expression \(-\cos x\) equals \(\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
questions.hint: Expand with the sine sum formula and substitute the sine and cosine of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a cosine of a supplementary angle using the difference formula.
questions.question: For every real \(x\), \(\cos(\pi-x)\) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: By the difference formula, \(\cos(\pi-x)=\cos\pi\cos x+\sin\pi\sin x=(-1)\cos x+0\cdot\sin x=-\cos x\). For example, \(\cos 120^\circ=-\cos 60^\circ\).
questions.hint: Expand with the cosine difference formula and substitute the values at \(\pi\).

questions.concept: Sine of a sum from given ratios
questions.learningObjective: Apply the sine sum formula after finding the missing sine and cosine.
questions.question: Acute angles \(A\) and \(B\) satisfy \(\sin A=\frac{3}{5}\) and \(\cos B=\frac{5}{13}\). What is \(\sin(A+B)\)?
questions.explanation: For acute angles, \(\cos A=\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\sin B=\frac{12}{13}\). Then \(\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B=\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{13}+\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{13}=\frac{15+48}{65}=\frac{63}{65}\). Pairing sine with sine and cosine with cosine gives \(\frac{36+20}{65}=\frac{56}{65}\), which is incorrect.
questions.hint: Find \(\cos A\) and \(\sin B\) first, then pair each sine with the cosine of the other angle.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a tangent exactly using the tangent difference formula.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\tan 15^\circ\)?
questions.hint: Use \(15^\circ=45^\circ-30^\circ\); the result must be less than \(1\) because \(15^\circ<45^\circ\).

questions.concept: Recognising a sum formula in reverse
questions.learningObjective: Condense an expression into a single sine using the sum formula.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\sin 20^\circ\cos 40^\circ+\cos 20^\circ\sin 40^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The expression has the form \(\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B\) with \(A=20^\circ\) and \(B=40^\circ\), so it equals \(\sin(20^\circ+40^\circ)=\sin 60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). The value \(\frac{1}{2}\) is \(\cos 60^\circ\), which would come from a cosine pattern instead.
questions.hint: Compare the expression with the expanded form of \(\sin(A+B)\).
